gaps.explanation: happen + to-infinitive = do something by chance: happen to know.
deny + -ing or having + past participle: denied doing/having done. Both accepted.

gaps.sentence: If you keep ___ like this, you'll exhaust yourself.
gaps.explanation: keep (+ on) is followed by -ing: keep working.

gaps.sentence: I saw him ___ the wall and disappear into the garden.
gaps.explanation: see/hear + object + bare infinitive = the complete action; -ing = the action in progress. Both readings possible here; the bare infinitive is expected.

gaps.sentence: It took me ages ___ used to the new keyboard.
gaps.explanation: it takes time + to-infinitive: took me ages to get used to the keyboard.

gaps.sentence: You'd better ___ a taxi or you'll miss the plane.
gaps.explanation: had better takes the bare infinitive: you'd better take.

gaps.sentence: I didn't mean ___ you — it was a joke.
gaps.explanation: mean (= intend) takes the to-infinitive: didn't mean to upset. (mean + -ing = involve.)
